claim: The paper plans Cartesian stiffness and damping online through constrained optimization that minimizes impedance-related cost while limiting perturbation-induced tracking error and respecting gain bounds, with an analytic solution for diagonally dominant inertia and a numerical solution otherwise, without force/torque sensing; it does not model the contacted environment or optimize from soft-contact mechanics.
epistemic_status: The optimization, experiments, and assumptions are author-reported; contact-model implications are bounded reader inferences.
problem_and_setting: Real-time selection of Cartesian impedance gains for robots under perturbations, with acceptable tracking-error and gain limits and no force/torque sensor requirement.
method_or_mechanism: A constrained optimization selects stiffness and damping, conservatively using minimum closed-loop inertia. It is analytic for diagonally dominant inertia and numerical for nondiagonal inertia. Perturbation attenuation enters through tracking-error constraints rather than an identified environment model.
content_summary: Quadruped and manipulator experiments compare variable gains with fixed gains and inertia shaping. Comparable performance is reported without force/torque sensors. Negligible Coriolis-like terms, slowly varying inertia, approximate gain bounds, and peak-impact energy modulation remain limitations or future work.
synthesis_role: Closest-prior evidence for online optimal impedance planning and a contact-agnostic baseline against which contact-state-aware planning must show decision-relevant benefit.
development_link: A soft-contact extension must show that measurable contact state or model uncertainty changes selected gains or improves outcomes beyond this planner under matched tracking-error and gain constraints.

evidence.finding: The method plans Cartesian impedance online without force/torque measurements and bounds perturbation effects.
It minimizes impedance-related cost subject to tracking-error and gain constraints, analytically for diagonal-dominant inertia and numerically otherwise.
Real-time robot experiments compare variable gains with fixed gains and a standard inertia-shaping method.
Comparable performance is reported without inertia shaping or force/torque sensors; slowly varying inertia, negligible Coriolis-like terms, and peak-impact energy modulation remain open.
Stiffness bounds and feasible-set construction are approximate design choices.

boundary_conditions: Analytic solution requires diagonally dominant inertia.
Coriolis-like terms are neglected and inertia is assumed slowly varying.
Tracking-error constraints replace explicit runtime contact-force constraints.
The feasible gain set is approximate.
No soft-tissue scanning or contact constitutive state is evaluated.
assumptions: Minimum closed-loop inertia is a suitable conservative choice.
Tracking-error limits encode acceptable perturbation effects.
Force/torque sensing is unnecessary for the stated objective.

reported: Non-negligible Coriolis-like terms and rapidly varying inertia are untreated.
Peak-impact kinetic-energy modulation is future work.
inferred: The planner cannot condition gains on relaxation, hysteresis, or pressure redistribution.
Tracking-error bounds do not imply hard force, pressure, deformation, or passivity bounds.
This baseline could falsify the need for richer contact state if held-out outcomes are indistinguishable.

conflicts_with: Any claim that online constrained Cartesian stiffness/damping optimization is new.
Any claim that force/torque sensing is universally required for useful online impedance planning.
Any equivalence between bounded tracking error and verified tissue-safety bounds.
